title: Responses interop shim: test harness & prioritized compatibility gap backlog
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: build a deterministic, automatable shim test harness that exercises the full OpenAI Responses API surface against Redwood's Responses-compatible endpoint and runtime, produce a conformance/gap matrix, and ship a prioritized backlog of runtime and adapter fixes with proposed fallbacks.

Scope: streaming tokens (including partial JSON/structured output boundaries), function/tool calling events and metadata, structured outputs (name/value objects, JSON blocks with schema), error/partial-failure modes, multipart tool outputs, role/channel mapping, and backwards-compatible semantics for prompt/system/message fields. This ticket covers test harness implementation, initial test corpus, triage & severity classification, and backlog handoff.

Why: multiple customer signups and internal integrations expect near-1:1 behavior with OpenAI Responses for streaming-tool sequences and structured outputs. Current ad-hoc tests found discrepancies in: chunked JSON reconstruction, tool-invocation ordering when combined with streaming, function argument shapes (camelCase vs snake_case), and stop-sequence handling during KV/prefix cache replay. These create subtle client-side parsing errors and user-facing regressions in agent workflows.

Success criteria: reproducible failing cases captured as automated tests, a clearly prioritized gap backlog with remediation owners and suggested runtime mitigations (e.g., local reassembly, tolerant parser modes, canonical field mapping), and merged test harness (CI + nightly conformance runs) that fails the build for high-severity regressions.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic harness repo (internal) that can run tests against both Redwood responses endpoint and a mocked OpenAI Responses fixture
A conformance matrix CSV/Confluence doc listing each test case, observed behavior, expected behavior, severity, and remediation suggestion
Automated CI job implementing nightly runs; high-severity mismatches create an alert and attach failing traces/requests
Backlog of prioritized fixes assigned to owners with proposed runtime fallbacks for P0/P1 gaps
At least 20 canonical test vectors covering streaming-tool interleavings, structured JSON streaming, and partial failure recovery
tasks: Design test harness API and runner (node/python) with pluggable 'target' implementations (redwood endpoint, openai fixture)
Create initial canonical test vectors: streaming JSON object split across tokens, tool-call then message tokenization, tool error + fallback, nested function calls
Implement reassembly verifier: reconstruct streaming chunks into final payload and compare strict/lenient modes
Run baseline audit against current runtime and capture diffs (store raw request/response/stream events)
Triage diffs, assign severity, add remediation proposals (adapter translation, runtime behavior changes, or client SDK tolerances)
Add CI pipeline: nightly run + failure artifact uploader (s3/internal dashboard), and Slack alerts for >=high severity
Write migration doc for SDK consumers describing known behavioral differences and recommended parser settings
